unit.subject: English
unit.unitOverview: In this unit you will learn how we travel and get around. You will meet the words for ways to travel — walk, bus, car, bicycle and boat — and learn to say how you go to school. You will talk about journeys: going somewhere with the people you love, staying safe, and enjoying the trip. Say the words out loud — this is about confident everyday English, not perfect spelling.
unit.learningPath:
Begin with the guided teacher launch and learn a few words through pictures and play.
Listen to the Unit story and join in with repeated language.
Complete the twelve language, speaking, early-writing and practical activities.
If you have access to live teacher sessions, meet your teacher three times each week for two weeks for extra practice — these are optional, and every skill in this unit is also fully covered through the teacher launch, story, and speaking and writing activities above.
Finish the ten-question checkpoint, then tell an adult what you can do if one is nearby — or say it out loud to yourself.

readings.title: Amal's Big Bus Ride
readings.setting: Home, online lesson or Grade 1 classroom
readings.passageScript:
Today, Amal was going to see her grandma. Grandma lived by the sea in a town far away.

“How will we get there?” asked Amal.

“First we walk. Then we go by bus,” said Mum. “Let's go!”

Amal and Mum walked down the road. They walked past the market. They walked to the bus stop.

Soon a big bus came. It was yellow and red. “Beep, beep!” went the bus.

“Find a seat. Then sit down,” said Mum. Amal found a seat by the window.

The wheels on the bus went round and round. The bus began to drive through the town.

“Look, Mum! A boy on a bicycle!” said Amal. The boy waved. His name was Adam.

“And look — a red car!” said Amal. The car went fast. But the bus went slow and bumpy.

Amal saw a girl named Samira, who was going to school. Samira waved too. Amal waved back.

The bus drove past the shops. It drove past the library. It drove all the way to the sea.

“We are here!” said Mum. At the sea, Amal saw a little blue boat. The boat could float on the water.

And there, by the boat, was Grandma! “Amal!” she called. “You came to see me!”

“Yes!” said Amal. She ran and gave Grandma a big hug.

“How did you travel here?” asked Grandma.

“We walked, and then we came by bus!” said Amal. “The wheels went round and round!”

Grandma smiled. “What a good journey. Now, shall we go on the boat?”

“Yes, yes!” said Amal. She held Grandma's hand. “Let's go!”

readings.passageScript:
“The Wheels on the Bus” — sing it together
The wheels on the bus go round and round, / round and round, round and round. / The wheels on the bus go round and round, / all day long!
Roll your hands round and round for the wheels. Then do more verses with actions: the wipers go “swish, swish, swish”, the bell goes “ding, ding, ding”. Sing it a little louder each time!

Bus driver, bus driver, / may I have a ride? / Yes, of course. / Please come inside. / Find a seat. / Then sit down. / Buckle up. / We'll drive through the town.
Take turns: you ask “May I have a ride?” and a grown-up answers. Pretend to find a seat, sit down and buckle up together.

grammar.title: Say how you travel
grammar.explanation: Tell us how you get to school each morning. Say the way you travel after the word 'by'.
grammar.commonMistake: 'I go by a bus' has an extra 'a'. After 'by' we say just the vehicle: 'by bus'.
grammar.memoryTip: Make the steering or pedalling action as you say the word after 'by'.
grammar.practice: Say three ways to travel: I go by bus. I go by car. I go by boat.

grammar.title: Say where a vehicle travels
grammar.explanation: Think about where each vehicle moves. A car goes on the road and a boat goes on the water.
grammar.commonMistake: Children may say 'It goes in the road.' Roads, water and tracks all take 'on'.
grammar.memoryTip: Slide your hand flat along the table. That is 'on'.
grammar.practice: Say three: It goes on the road. It goes on the water. It goes on the tracks.

grammar.title: Name what you see on the journey
grammar.explanation: Name one thing you spot on the trip. Say 'a' before most words, but 'an' before a vowel sound: a bus, an aeroplane.
grammar.commonMistake: Children pop 'a' before aeroplane by mistake. Before an a, e, i, o, u sound we say 'an': an aeroplane, an ambulance.
grammar.memoryTip: Open-mouth sound at the start — a, e, i, o, u — means you say 'an'.
grammar.practice: Say three you pass: I can see a bus. I can see an aeroplane. I can see a bridge.

grammar.title: Say which vehicle is fast
grammar.explanation: Choose a quick vehicle and tell us about it. You can try the word 'slow' too.
grammar.commonMistake: 'The train fast' is missing 'is'. Every describing sentence needs 'is' in the middle.
grammar.memoryTip: Zoom your hand past quickly whenever you say 'fast'.
grammar.practice: Say three: The train is fast. The plane is fast. The bike is slow.

grammar.title: Say what we are doing together
grammar.explanation: Use 'we' when you and other people do something. Add -ing to the action word.
grammar.commonMistake: Children often say 'We is walking.' The word 'we' always takes 'are': 'We are walking.'
grammar.memoryTip: Circle your arm around the whole group when you say 'we'.
grammar.practice: Say three group actions: We are walking. We are waiting. We are riding.

grammar.title: Tell a journey in two steps
grammar.explanation: Describe your trip in order. Say the first step, then say what happens next.
grammar.commonMistake: The two steps can come out backwards. Ask 'What did you do first?' before saying the sentence.
grammar.memoryTip: Step forward once for 'first' and once more for 'then'.
grammar.practice: Say three journeys: First we walk, then we take the bus. First we wait, then we get on. First we pay, then we sit down.

grownUpGuide.label: Teacher & Parent Guide
grownUpGuide.intro: In this unit, your child learns how we travel and get around. They meet the words for ways to travel (walk, bus, car, bicycle, boat) and learn to say how they go to school. They talk about journeys — going somewhere with the people they love, staying safe, and enjoying the trip. The goal is warm, confident English about the everyday world of going places — not perfect spelling.

sections.title: 🧭 About this unit (please read first)
sections.body:
Your child is a beginner, about 5–7 years old, and is just starting to read. So YOU lead this unit — a teacher in class or a parent at home.

Work in short, happy sessions of about 15–20 minutes. Lots of pointing, saying, singing, colouring and playing — very little writing.

This guide tells you what to do. The Child Activity Sheet is what your child draws and colours. The Story is one you read aloud.

sections.title: 💬 Using the AI Tutor with a young child
sections.body:
The grown-up holds the device and reads with the child — do not leave a 5-year-old alone with it.

Ask the tutor to say a word slowly so your child can copy the sound: “Please say the word ‘bicycle’ slowly.”

Ask it to sing “The Wheels on the Bus”, or to make the sound of a bus, a car and a boat for you to guess.

Ask it to give you one more simple travel activity if your child wants to keep going.

sections.title: 🌟 Tips for teaching absolute beginners
sections.body:
Keep it short and playful. Stop while it is still fun.

Repeat, repeat, repeat — young children learn by hearing words many times.

Use your hands, face and voice. Make the engine noises and do the actions.

Praise every try. Confidence matters more than being correct at this stage.

sections.title: What Your Child Will Be Able to Do

sections.title: Songs and Rhymes
sections.body:
“The Wheels on the Bus” — sing it together

The wheels on the bus go round and round, / round and round, round and round. / The wheels on the bus go round and round, / all day long!

Roll your hands round and round for the wheels. Then do more verses with actions: the wipers go “swish, swish, swish”, the bell goes “ding, ding, ding”. Sing it a little louder each time!

“Bus Driver, Bus Driver” — a little rhyme

Bus driver, bus driver, / may I have a ride? / Yes, of course. / Please come inside. / Find a seat. / Then sit down. / Buckle up. / We'll drive through the town.

Take turns: your child asks “May I have a ride?” and you answer. Pretend to find a seat, sit down and buckle up together.

sections.title: How to Teach This Unit, Step by Step
sections.body:
Repeat this simple shape over several short sessions:

1. Warm-up (2–3 min)

Greet your child: “Hello! Are you ready to go?”

Sing “The Wheels on the Bus” together.

2. Learn the words (5 min)

Point to a picture or toy vehicle and say the word clearly: “bus”. Ask your child to repeat.

Do 4–5 words at a time. Make the sound and the action — “drive” (hold the wheel), “fly” (arms out).

3. Play and sing (5 min)

Travel sorting game: name a vehicle and ask “Does it go on land, on water, or in the sky?”

Pretend journey: line up chairs as a “bus”, buckle up, and drive through the town.

4. Story time (5 min)

Read the Story file, “Sagal's Big Bus Ride”, aloud. Point to the bold words and to the pictures your child has drawn, and ask the simple talk-about questions.

5. Activity sheet (5 min)

Sit with your child and do one or two activities from the Child Activity Sheet. Read each instruction aloud for them.

6. Wrap-up (2 min)

Ask: “How do YOU like to travel?” Celebrate! Say “Well done!” and one thing they did well.

sections.title: Sentence Patterns to Say Out Loud
sections.body: Speaking comes before writing. Practise these spoken patterns often:
items: “I go to school by ______.” (bus, car, bicycle, foot)
“Let's go!”
“It is a ______.” (a bus, a car, a boat)
“It goes ______.” (fast, slow, round and round)
“I can ______.” (walk, ride, drive, fly, float)

sections.title: Simple Check — What to Look For
sections.body: You do not need a test. Just watch and tick when your child can do these:
items: Points to and names 5 ways to travel.
Says how they get to school: “I go to school by ______.”
Says a colour and size for a vehicle: “a big red bus.”
Joins in “The Wheels on the Bus” with actions.
Says one action: “I can ______.” (ride, drive, fly, float)
